chunk_findings.detail: The handler unconditionally does `bug.invalid_at = bug.invalid_reason = bug.evidence = ""`, but `evidence` is not an invalid-only field: `_h_bug_found` sets `bug.evidence = ev.data.get("evidence", "")`, i.e. it holds the evidence the reporter attached when the bug was *found*. Concrete scenario: `bug found B1 --evidence "traceback in parse()"` (record now has `evidence="traceback in parse()"`), then `bug.fixed B1` (fixed_at/regression_test/lesson set, `evidence` untouched), then a `bug.reopened B1 --reason "closure was from the completion sweep"` whose event data has no `evidence` key. Line `_h_bug_reopened` sets `bug.evidence = ""`, so the reopened record no longer contains why the bug was originally filed, even though the docstring's stated contract is only to "undo a closure" and the found event is still in the log. Undoing a fix should leave the record in its pre-fix state (which had `evidence` set), so the reset should be scoped to the invalid fields (`invalid_at`, `invalid_reason`) rather than clearing the found-time evidence (or it should re-populate evidence from the found event). The same wipe also silently destroys the found evidence when reopening an invalid bug, since nothing restores it.

chunk_findings.detail: The change makes `_fix_task` return an ABANDONED task as the bug's fix task, and the CLI now tells the user that this bug "needs a new task to fix it" — but the only documented mechanism for producing that new task, `bug file-tasks`, is triggered by exactly the empty string that `_fix_task` no longer returns (the docstring kept in this diff still states: "'' when no task was filed to fix it ..., so `bug file-tasks` files one"; the change even justifies naming the abandoned task with "`bug file-tasks` would link straight back to it"). Concretely: `ddflow bug invalid Bx` abandons `fix-Bx`; then `ddflow bug reopen Bx` (the scenario the added test encodes) reports `fix_task=fix-Bx`, `fix_task_state=abandoned`; now `ddflow bug file-tasks` sees the bug as already having a fix task (non-empty `_fix_task`) and will not file a fresh one, and `bug_reopen` does not un-abandon `fix-Bx` either. The DONE remedy offered by the sibling branch (`ddflow verify <task> --reopen`) is not offered for ABANDONED, so the reopened bug is left with no open fix task and no documented way to get one. The added regression test asserts only the label ("abandoned" in the output) and never checks that a fix task can actually be produced after the reopen, so it locks in this dead end.

chunk_findings.detail: `refile_reported` refiles every open bug whose `fix_task == item`, but it has no test of the bug's scope. The change's own intent is that `scope=ddflow` upstream reports (e.g. B6620834d85, Bc507dd65bf, B0f132adaed, filed against `fix-B297ede2447` with `--item`) must be *excluded* from the completion sweep; the function instead treats them exactly like locally-fixable bugs. Concretely, given an item `fix-B7bdcc6b212` and an open bug `Bx` with `scope == "ddflow"` and `fix_task == "fix-B7bdcc6b212"`, completing the item takes the `b is None or not b.open or b.fix_task != item` guard as "process", calls `_file_fix_task(... item=item, ...)` and appends `bug.found Bx {"fix_task": "fix-Bx"}`. The upstream report therefore comes out of completion owning a bogus local `fix-<bug>` task (and `bug reopen Bx` will afterwards report "fix task: fix-Bx", pointing the user at a task nobody filed to fix it), which is the harm the exclusion was supposed to prevent. Note the code does implement the sibling exclusion (bugs whose fix task is a different item, via `b.fix_task != item`) but omits the `scope=ddflow` one.

chunk_findings.detail: The `get` default falls back to the bug's *current* `fix_task`, which after the wrongful closure described in B7bdcc6b212 is exactly the item that has just been completed (e.g. `fix-B297ede2447`). This handler exists to undo that closure (`api/bug_reopen` emits `bug.reopened`), and the field docstring added in this same diff says `fix_task` is "what the writer decided …, `""` when the old one cannot fix it" — i.e. clearing the stale task must be the default, not preserving it. Given a `bug.reopened` event whose payload carries no `fix_task` key (the natural encoding for a report that has no open fix task of its own and must end up with `fix_task == ""`), the line leaves `fix_task` pointing at the completed item. The reopened bug therefore still matches `CM.reported_against`/`open_bugs_of` on a done task — the exact "stranded on a done task" state the comment at `api/lifecycle.py:1469` promises never occurs — and any later sweep that keys on `fix_task` can re-close it. The `or ""` in the expression is dead weight unless the intent was `ev.data.get("fix_task", "")`; writing it as `str(ev.data.get("fix_task", bug.fix_task) or "")` makes the fallback the one value (the just-closed item) that can no longer fix the bug.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/model.py:_h_bug_reopened (`bug.fix_task = str(ev.data.get("fix_task", bug.fix_task) or "")`)

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert any("Bflake" in w and "Bup" in w for w in out.data["warnings"])` requires a *single* warning string to contain both refiled bug ids. But the warning is emitted once per bug: the sibling test in the same file (`test_with_file_task_off_the_reports_stay_open_and_the_warning_says_no_task`, and likewise `test_a_bug_reported_against...`'s own comment "Said out loud: the reports stay open and are not this task's to close") matches the warning template `"bug <id> ... ; <detail>"` containing exactly one bug id plus a per-bug detail ("filed fix-<id>" / "files no fix task"). In this test two bugs (Bup and Bflake) are reported against `fix-Bx`, so two separate warnings are produced — one naming Bup, one naming Bflake — and no element `w` of `warnings` contains both substrings. The predicate is therefore False and the test fails even though the completion behaviour (both reports stay open, both get refiled) is correct. The check needs to be `any("Bflake" in w for w in warnings) and any("Bup" in w for w in warnings)` (or an aggregate assertion if the implementation really does concatenate all ids into one warning, which the per-bug template contradicts).

chunk_findings.detail: The stated intent is to fix B7bdcc6b212, whose core defect is that `ddflow complete <item>` sweeps up *every* open bug filed against that item — including `scope=ddflow` upstream reports and bugs whose fix task is a different item — marking them fixed even though nothing was fixed, with no way to reopen. The suggested fixes are: warn when a bug is filed against an item completion will close, exclude `scope=ddflow` bugs and bugs whose fix task is a different item from the completion sweep, and provide a reopen. This diff contains none of that. Its only functional content is a rewording of the "abandoned fix task" guidance string in `_next_step` (plus the matching `in` assertion in the test) and a docstring paraphrase; the completion-sweep selection logic, the filing-time warning, and any reopen path are untouched. Concretely: create item `T`, file bugs `B_a` (scope=ddflow) and `B_b` (whose fix task is a separate item `fix-B_b`) against it, then run `ddflow complete T`; after applying this change those bugs are still closed by the sweep exactly as before, so the reported failure scenario for B7bdcc6b212 still reproduces. The change therefore does not deliver the fix it claims.

The new test does not exercise the behavior this change modifies, so it cannot be the "watch it FAIL on the unfixed code" regression test the intent requires. Its inputs are `_rec(f"U{i}", "orphan_worktree", None)` and `_rec(f"S{i}", "stale_running", False)`. Trace the pre-image function that is replaced by `_recovery_band`:

```

    if r.salvageable is None:  # False, since it is False, not None
```
